gallery.credit: Robert N. Dennis collection of stereoscopic views, New York Public Library. Digital ID: G91F171_020F Record ID: 755158 Catalog Call Number: MFY Dennis Coll 91-F171
gallery.description: The Brooklyn Theatre before the catastrophic fire on December 05, 1876. Furthest from the camera, behind the tree, is the Dieter Hotel. The theater has a tall, mansard roof. Next door to the right is the First Precinct Station House. The U. S. Post Office is further to the right.
categories: Post offices in Brooklyn, New York City

gallery.title: File:Brooklyn Theatre Floor Plan 1.png
gallery.credit: New York Tribune Thursday, December 07, 1876 Vol. XXXVI No., 11,136 Page 1. This is the ground floor plan and does not show the seating in the second and third floor galleries. See "Brooklyn Theatre Floor Plan 2" for the lobby and vestibule detail, and the stairway plan to the highest tier, where the majority of the fatalities occurred.
gallery.description: Floor Plan of the Brooklyn Theatre. Published on Thursday, 07-December-1876 in the New York Tribune

gallery.credit: New York Tribune Thursday, December 07, 1876 Vol. XXXVI No., 11,136 Page 1.
gallery.description: New York Tribune Thursday, December 07, 1876 Vol. XXXVI No., 11,136 Page 1. This is a detail of the vestibule and lobby showing the arrangement of stairs to the upper galleries. Note that this diagram is rotated counter-clockwise 90 degrees with respect to Plan 1.

gallery.filename: Brooklyn Theatre Lot Sanborn Map Detail.png
gallery.title: File:Brooklyn Theatre Lot Sanborn Map Detail.png
gallery.credit: Insurance Maps Brooklyn NY Volume 2. Published by the Sanborn Map Publishing Company, 117 Broadway, New York, NY 1887. Detail from  double page plate No. 40 [Map bounded by Pearl St., Boerum Place, State St., Clinton St., Pierrepont St., Fulton St., Johnson St.]
gallery.source: Brooklyn Theatre Lot Sanborn Map Detail
gallery.description: Excerpt from double page plate 40 of the Sanborn Brooklyn Maps, Volume Two, 1887 edition, with a highlight on the lot occupied by the Brooklyn Theatre. The structure in the lot is not the original theatre, but a new building erected two years after the fire. The new theatre fit in the same lot as the original, but its internal layout was wholly unlike the original Brooklyn Theatre.
